line_texts: We study how fixed-size queues between the stages of a document
processing pipeline waste memory under bursty input. A feedback
controller that resizes each buffer from observed queue depth keeps
tail latency within 8% of the optimum while using 41% less memory.

line_texts: 本文研究文档处理流水线各阶段之间的固定长度队列在突发输入下浪费内存的问题，

将内存占用降低了四成以上。

line_texts: Modern pipelines split a job into stages such as parsing, layout and
rendering, and connect them with bounded queues. When the arrival rate
exceeds the service rate $\mu_k$ of a stage, its queue grows until the
bound is hit and upstream stages stall. Choosing a single bound for all
inputs is therefore a compromise between memory use and throughput.
content.text: Modern pipelines split a job into stages such as parsing, layout and rendering, and connect them with bounded queues. Choosing a single bound for all inputs is therefore a compromise between memory use and throughput.

line_texts: Resizing buffers from observed queue depth removes most of the memory
cost of burst tolerance at a small latency price. We plan to extend the
controller to stages that share a common memory pool.
